articles.title: Certificate authority keys: eMudhra's browser and runtime trust gap
articles.excerpt: The eMudhra certificate authority incident has an awkward developer-facing cleanup problem. Browser vendors can block a compromised certificate chain while a deployed application keeps reading an olde…
articles.body: The eMudhra certificate authority incident has an awkward developer-facing cleanup problem. Browser vendors can block a compromised certificate chain while a deployed application keeps reading an older CA bundle. Eight intermediate signing keys were compromised, and your browser's update history cannot tell you which trust material a containerized service has loaded. The place to close the incident is the deployed client's actual validation path. TL;DR Mozilla's incident report identifies eight compromised intermediate signing keys: six for TLS and two for code signing. A compromised intermediate key gives its holder signing authority under that certificate. Mozilla independently recovered the affected keys.
articles.author: Nikoloz Turazashvili (@axrisi)

articles.title: We measured 0.0000 % and it proved nothing: how do you observe a default that never fires?
articles.excerpt: We built a checker for our generated visuals and, on our flagship case, the pixel share of the "default color" was 0.0000 % - 0 of 921,600 pixels. We almost called the rule wrong. It wasn't wrong. It…
articles.body: We built a checker for our generated visuals and, on our flagship case, the pixel share of the "default color" was 0.0000 % - 0 of 921,600 pixels. We almost called the rule wrong. It wasn't wrong. It was unobservable . In that configuration the base color is set explicitly (897 mentions), so the default path never enters the frame. The instrument was fine; our expectation was formed on the wrong surface. Two questions for people who build these pipelines: Which configuration of yours leaves the base color unset , so the default path is visible at all? We need one counter-case to settle the rule in either direction.

articles.title: Is That Really GPTBot? How to Find and Verify AI Crawlers in Your Server Logs
articles.excerpt: You've allowed AI search bots in robots.txt. Great. But are they actually reaching your pages, and are the requests in your logs really from them? The User-Agent header is just a string. Anyone can se…
articles.body: You've allowed AI search bots in robots.txt . Great. But are they actually reaching your pages, and are the requests in your logs really from them? The User-Agent header is just a string. Anyone can send GPTBot in a curl request. So "I saw GPTBot in my logs" proves very little until you check two things: what status code the bot got and whether the IP really belongs to the vendor . This guide shows how to do both with standard tools: grep , awk and a short Python script. 1. Know which bots you're looking for Major AI vendors now separate bots by purpose. This matters, because blocking the wrong one can quietly remove you from AI search answers.

articles.excerpt: How Word Games Turn a Random Set of Letters Into Meaningful Words Have you ever looked at a group of scrambled letters and wondered how many words you could make from them? Word games make this proces…
articles.body: How Word Games Turn a Random Set of Letters Into Meaningful Words Have you ever looked at a group of scrambled letters and wondered how many words you could make from them? Word games make this process look simple. You enter a few letters, and within seconds, you might find several possible words. But behind that simple experience are interesting problems involving data structures, search algorithms, and user interface design. Understanding these concepts is useful if you want to build a word game, a vocabulary application, or a small browser-based puzzle. Let's look at how the process works.

articles.title: TCP: cómo CUBIC y BBR controlan la congestión de red
articles.excerpt: Cuando subís un archivo grande y la velocidad cae a la mitad apenas otra persona abre un video en la misma red, no es magia: es el control de congestión TCP decidiendo, paquete a paquete, cuánto tráfi…
articles.body: Cuando subís un archivo grande y la velocidad cae a la mitad apenas otra persona abre un video en la misma red, no es magia: es el control de congestión TCP decidiendo, paquete a paquete, cuánto tráfico puede soportar el enlace antes de perder datos. Linux permite cambiar el algoritmo que toma esa decisión con un solo comando, y la diferencia entre CUBIC (el que usás hoy sin saberlo) y BBR (el que diseñó Google en 2016) se mide en milisegundos de latencia y megabits por segundo reales.

articles.title: One zone lost power in London, and the banks went dark with it
articles.excerpt: Tuesday, just after 7am Tuesday morning in London. People tapped their bank cards at the till and the payment was declined. Revolut transfers froze mid-send. Lloyds and HSBC customers could not get in…
articles.body: Tuesday, just after 7am Tuesday morning in London. People tapped their bank cards at the till and the payment was declined. Revolut transfers froze mid-send. Lloyds and HSBC customers could not get into their apps. In courts across England and Wales, video hearings stalled because the courts' video platform was down. Royal Mail tracking went quiet, and delivery networks wobbled. None of these companies had a power cut. A Google Cloud data center zone did. Just after 7am London time on Tuesday, October 20, a power event knocked out europe-west2-b, one of three availability zones inside Google Cloud's London region. Google's own status text put it plainly: "A power event caused an outage within europe-west2-b zone. The power event is mitigated." What followed is the part worth studying.

articles.title: Why I Built a Mortgage Calculator That Doesn't Track You (100% Client-Side)
articles.excerpt: As developers, we build tools to solve problems. But when I was looking for a mortgage calculator for my own personal use, I noticed a disturbing trend: almost every calculator out there requires you…
articles.body: As developers, we build tools to solve problems. But when I was looking for a mortgage calculator for my own personal use, I noticed a disturbing trend: almost every calculator out there requires you to sign up, give your email, or worse, they track your financial data and sell it to third parties. That didn't sit right with me. Financial data is deeply personal. So, I decided to build my own: Smart Mortgage Calc . Here is why I built it, the tech stack I used, and the challenges of building financial tools in the browser. The Core Problem: Privacy When you input your income, your down payment, and your desired loan amount into a standard calculator, where does that data go? Usually, it's sent to a server, stored in a database, and used for targeted advertising.

articles.excerpt: NASA has updated the timeline for its Artemis III mission and mapped out the expected progress for SpaceX and Blue Origin's respective moon landers.
articles.body: NASA has revealed new details about its plans to return astronauts to the surface of the moon, outlining a series of upcoming milestones for SpaceX and Blue Origin as both companies race to ready their lunar landers for the agency's Artemis program . During an Oct. 5 presentation at the Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Antalya, Türkiye, Steve Creech, acting manager of NASA's Human Landing System (HLS) Program, laid out development timelines for both spacecraft, with key demonstrations planned through early 2028 that include orbital refueling and uncrewed lunar landing tests to qualify the vehicles to fly astronauts to the surface of the moon . A more pressing deadline, however, is NASA's Artemis III mission, which is targeted for the third quarter (Q3) of 2027.
